name: Cross and Crescent: The Crusades
description: Two centuries of holy war over Jerusalem: popes, kings, knights, sultans and merchants, and the fortresses and orders that came out of them.

checkpoints.name: The call to arms
checkpoints.note: After the Seljuk Turks beat the Byzantines at Manzikert, the emperor asked the West for help. Christian kingdoms in Spain were already fighting Muslim rulers in the Reconquista. At Clermont, Pope Urban II preached a pilgrimage in arms to the Holy Land.

checkpoints.name: The First Crusade and the new states
checkpoints.note: Crusaders took Jerusalem in 1099 and founded the Kingdom of Jerusalem. Orders like the Hospitallers and Templars were formed, and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre was the goal of pilgrims.

checkpoints.name: Saladin and Richard
checkpoints.note: Saladin united Muslim lands and won at Hattin, retaking Jerusalem. Richard I and others answered in the Third Crusade, and strongholds like Krak des Chevaliers watched the roads.

checkpoints.name: Detours and orders
checkpoints.note: The Fourth Crusade sacked Christian Constantinople, damaging its walls and the Byzantine Empire. Francis of Assisi preached peace and met a sultan, and the Teutonic Order looked north.

checkpoints.name: The last states fall
checkpoints.note: The Mamluks of Egypt took power, and the Mongols were beaten at Ain Jalut. The last crusader cities on the coast fell by 1291, ending the crusader states, and the knightly orders had to find new homes.
